issues.legal_issue: Enforcement after a constitutional judgment of a law protected from fundamental-rights challenge by its inclusion in a constitutional schedule remains immune from challenge on the ground that the enforcement infringes fundamental rights.
material_facts: The petitioner was directed to show cause why land held in excess of the ceiling should not be treated as surplus and vest in the State under an agricultural land-ceiling law.
The law had been included in the constitutional schedule before the earlier judgment relied on by the petitioner.
The petitioner argued that enforcement after that judgment could be challenged for infringing fundamental rights.
The challenged enforcement occurred after the earlier judgment.
issues.conclusion: The petitioner could not challenge the action on the ground that it was taken after the earlier judgment, and the petition was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the majority in I. C. Golaknath v. State of Punjab (1967) treated laws included in the Ninth Schedule as protected by Article 31B from challenge for infringing Part III rights. The prospective operation of that judgment did not make action taken after its delivery under amendments made before then invalid on fundamental-rights grounds. The Court also relied on State of Maharashtra v. Madhavrao Damodar Patilchand (1968), which had upheld the validity of the agricultural land-ceiling law as amended.

predicates.constitutional_writ_challenging_enforcem: A person brought a constitutional writ proceeding to challenge enforcement of a law against them.
predicates.schedule_protection_preceded_prior_judgm: The law had been placed within a constitutional schedule that protects it from fundamental-rights challenges before the earlier judgment relied on by the person.
predicates.fundamental_rights_infringement_alleged: The person alleged that enforcement of the law infringed fundamental rights.
predicates.enforcement_followed_prior_judgment: The challenged enforcement occurred after the earlier judgment relied on by the person.
predicates.challenge_to_enforcement_rejected: The challenge to enforcement on the asserted fundamental-rights ground is rejected.

issues.definition: When a constitutional writ challenges enforcement after an earlier judgment of a law already protected by schedule inclusion, alleging infringement of fundamental rights, the challenge is rejected.
